text: Someone stole the Mona Lisa. And for a whole day, nobody noticed.
Paris, 1911. A Monday. The Louvre is closed.
Vincenzo Peruggia, a house painter, is inside, dressed in a museum workman's white smock.
He lifts her off four hooks, wraps her in the smock, and walks out.
The guards see the gap and shrug: the photographers must have her.
Next morning an artist comes to paint her, and finds only hooks.
Sixty detectives search. Even Pablo Picasso is questioned. Wrong man.
When the Louvre reopens, thousands queue to stare at an empty wall.
For two years she lies in a trunk in Peruggia's room.
Then he offers her to a dealer in Florence, in a letter signed Leonardo, and is arrested.
In January 1914 she is back on her hooks.
And the theft helped make her the most famous painting on Earth.
